A fits the current code better because the setting would follow the same path every existing setting already uses. `settings/resolver.ts:12` owns the defaults, and the traced data path delivers resolved values to `ui/report-view.ts:30`. The view therefore gets this setting the same way it gets the others. A view-local settings object would create a second source of settings beside the resolver. That means a second place to define defaults and a value the view reads that other settings code never sees. Ownership stays with the resolver, and I'll record that answer in the draft.

Next is what the setting should do on a workspace switch, since the reported problem is filters carrying over and hiding rows in the new workspace.

A) The setting decides whether filters reset on a workspace switch, and it defaults to reset.
B) The setting decides whether filters reset on a workspace switch, and it defaults to keep, so today's behavior stays unless a user opts in.
C) Filters always reset on a workspace switch, and the setting covers some other report-view preference. If so, name that preference.
D) other - name it

Recommendation: A - resetting by default fixes the hidden rows you reported. Anyone who wants filters to carry over can still turn that on through the same resolver path.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
A fits because `settings/resolver.ts:12` already owns defaults, and `ui/report-view.ts:30` already consumes its resolved settings. Reusing that path gives the new setting one authoritative default and avoids a separate view-local settings object that could drift from the resolver.

That settles ownership, but not what should happen to filters when switching workspaces. Which behavior do you want?
A) Always clear report filters on workspace changes; no setting is needed.
B) Make it configurable, clearing filters by default.
C) Make it configurable, preserving filters by default.
D) Other - name it.
Recommendation: B - it addresses hidden rows by default while allowing users to retain filters intentionally.
